title: Medicare Card Scam Calls
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying you need a new card or your benefits will stop. They try to get your Medicare number or other personal details.
example_message: "This is Medicare calling. We need to send you a new card. Please confirm your Medicare number and address."
red_flags: Unsolicited call about your Medicare card
Threats that your benefits will end
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer warning of a virus or security problem. It urges you to call a phone number, where scammers ask for remote access or payment.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Asked to call a number right away
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number; real tech companies do not use pop-ups to contact you.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer, saying your grandchild is in trouble and needs money fast. They ask you to keep it a secret.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in jail and need bail money. Please don’t tell mom and dad—can you send $2,000 right away?"
red_flags: Asked to keep it a secret
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check the story.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying there’s a problem with a package delivery and you need to click a link to fix it. The link leads to a fake website that steals your info.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to update your address: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link to click for more info
Requests for personal or payment info
what_to_do: Do not click the link; check your orders directly with the delivery company.

title: Social Security Suspension Scam
how_it_works: Scammers call or email saying your Social Security number is suspended due to suspicious activity. They threaten arrest or loss of benefits unless you pay or provide information.
example_message: "This is the Social Security Administration. Your number has been suspended. Press 1 to speak to an agent or your benefits will be stopped."
red_flags: Threats of arrest or loss of benefits
Asked to pay with gift cards or wire transfer
what_to_do: Hang up and do not give out any information; contact Social Security directly if you’re concerned.
